title: Tianwan moves step closer to becoming world's biggest nuclear power plant
html:
The fuel for the VVER-1200 reactor was supplied from the Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant by Rosatom's fuel division, TVEL, for the nuclear power plant, which is on China's coast in Jiangsu Province.

The fuel includes the initial core load and a reserve batch of fuel assemblies.

When the eighth unit is operational, Tianwan will have about 9.1 GW of installed capacity, which will not only make it the largest-capacity nuclear power plant in the world, but will also put it in the top 10 of all power plants.

The largest nuclear power plants, ranked by operable capacity

1: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa - 7 units operable - 8.2 GW
2: Tianwan - 7 units operable - 7.9 GW
3: Hongyanhe - 6 units operable - 6.7 GW
4: Fuqing - 6 units operable - 6.7 GW
5: Yangjiang - 6 units operable - 6.5 GW

Anton Ivanov, Vice President for Commerce and International Business at TVEL, said the past year in China had seen a record volume of nuclear fuel supplied to a single country: "Since late 2025, we have already delivered three complete VVER-1200 core loads - for Units 7 and 8 at Tianwan and for Unit 3 at Xudapu. By the end of 2026, the initial fuel load for Unit 4 at Xudapu will be manufactured and accepted by the customer."

In addition to the delivery of the fuel, China National Nuclear Power, a subsidiary of China National Nuclear Corporation, has also announced that on Wednesday it completed hot tests at the new unit successfully.

These tests aim to verify the reliability of equipment on the nuclear and conventional parts of the plant, ensuring that the systems and equipment meet design requirements.

The background

The first four units at the Tianwan site - which began commercial operation between June 2007 and December 2018 - are Gidropress VVER units supplied by Russia. Units 5 and 6 both feature Chinese ACPR1000 reactors.

In June 2018, Russia and China signed agreements for the construction of two VVER-1200 reactors as units 7 and 8 of the Tianwan plant. Construction of unit 7 began in May 2021, with that of unit 8 starting in February 2022. The units were scheduled to be put into commercial operation in 2026 and 2027, respectively.

The Tianwan nuclear power plant is owned and operated by Jiangsu Nuclear Power Company, a joint venture between CNNC (50%), China Power Investment Corporation (30%) and Jiangsu Guoxin Group (20%).


(Image: CNNC)

In January, CNNC announced that hot tests - which simulate the temperatures and pressures the reactor systems will be subjected to during normal operation - had been completed at unit 7 on 30 December. Cold tests - which verify the leak-tightness of the primary circuit and components - were completed at unit 8 in October. Unit 7 is expected to enter commercial operation "within the year".

Once all units at the Tianwan plant are operational, the total installed capacity will exceed 9 GWe, with an annual power generation of over 70 TWh, reducing carbon dioxide emissions by 57.4 million tonnes annually.
summary: Hot tests have been completed and the initial fuel load delivered for Tianwan unit 8. When all eight units at the site in China are up and running it will become the world's largest nuclear power plant.
